reworkSamples.finding: o1 is an editorial occasion line in a volume explicitly compiled by the named disciple Jiyun (寂蘊編), not an unnameable compiler; o4 is likewise in a volume explicitly compiled by Longqi and others (隆琦等編). The six-rung conclusions and source notes are therefore false.

o5 is the compiler's occasion label 普茶，示眾 followed by the record master's direct speech, while o3 is an occasion label 一晚普茶次 before Chaozong's raising of Yunmen. The entry must distinguish the narrator-governed occasion from the subsequent master's utterance instead of assigning one voice to the whole stored span.

The definition 'communal tea' holds, but the explanation names Ruibai Mingxue as addressing the assembly at the retreat tea while the headword itself occurs in Jiyun's occasion line. Rewrite the claim so speaker and occasion-label evidence are unambiguous.
o6 is in the signed preface 汾陽無德禪師語錄序 by Yang Yi (楊億述), so 'the reviewed unnamed compiler' is demonstrably wrong. It is authored preface prose describing Xuefeng's responsive eye.

o1 is a 頌曰 verse in a case-and-verse collection and requires recovery of the verse voice or an honest collection-level verse attribution; it is not established as compiler narrative by the generic six-rung sentence.

o4 supplies the corpus's explicit graph-level definition 子啐母啄，啄與啐不先不後，是為同時 and supports the paired-pecking sense. Preserve it, but make the prose's response/timing inference traceable to this occurrence rather than treating all six genres as equivalent.
o2 sits in the section 福州雪峰大智禪師 and the exact insult is spoken by that section master; assigning it to Xuefeng Yicun conflates two different Xuefeng masters.

o5 is uttered inside a later master's extended discussion ('不見古人道：這漆桶，或云野狐精...'), not by Mazu Daoyi merely because the surrounding anthology section eventually discusses Mazu. The exact-turn attribution fails.

o4 and o6 are later commentary/collection voices on the Puyan-Puxian case and remain generically assigned to an unnamed compiler despite recoverable named commentators around the passage. Re-resolve the exact quoted voice and separate original saying from later appraisal where a span contains both.

'Wild-fox spirit' and its use as an insult/verdict hold. 'Playing a deceptive fox-spirit rather than meeting the case cleanly' exceeds the stored wording; describe the observable rebuke and accused 見解 without assigning a psychological or evaluative theory to every occurrence.
o2 contains the headword in the paratext title 題東坡居士大悲閣記. It is an editorial/title occurrence, not an utterance by Yuanwu Keqin, and cannot carry him as MasterName under the utterer-only rule.

o1 and o4 narrate the same Dongpo-Foyin robe exchange in two compilation works. Their headword is compiler narration naming Dongpo as a case figure; the generic unnamed-compiler labels need real source-specific actor evidence and ContextMasters/case-figure roles.

o3 is narrative about a master raising Dongpo's verse, whereas o5 is This'an Shoujing directly saying and judging 東坡居士 in a formal address. Preserve that genre distinction instead of presenting all occurrences as an undifferentiated record of Dongpo's own questions and verses.

o6 contains 法衣 only in the compiler's occasion heading 施主獻法衣上堂; Dongshan Liangjie begins speaking after that heading and does not utter the headword. MasterName therefore violates the exact-utterer rule.

o3 is imperial-bestowal biographical narration (敕賜金襴法衣), while o4-o5 are transmission biographies and o1-o2 are direct masters displaying or lifting a robe. The current single gloss 'the teaching robe' and prose collapse monastic/ceremonial robe, bestowed honor, and lineage-transmission token without testing whether these are different things under sense-split rule 8.

Re-adjudicate the sense boundary and make each institutional claim rest on the corresponding occurrence; possession of a 法衣 is not shown in these six passages as one uniform assertion of possession of the teaching.
o1 is authored discourse 尊火為宗論 in Juelang Daosheng's record, and o2 is Langting Ting's direct 小參 address; both are wrongly reduced to 'the reviewed unnamed compiler.'
o3 is a signed 後序 by Nanqian (住堯封寶雲院嗣法門人南潛謹書), not an unnamed compiler. Its historical comparison of Fuxi and writing must name that author and keep him distinct from the masters discussed.

The figure sense holds, but 'what precedes conventional patterning' is not a shared deployment across the selected evidence: the passages use Fuxi for fire/cosmology, the sixty-four hexagrams, the institution of writing, primordial beginnings, and revealed signs. Rewrite as an evidence-bounded range rather than one inferred function.

o1 is continuous doctrinal address in the old recorded sayings, not established as compiler narration merely because the local head lookup is empty. The complete discourse/container ladder must resolve the speaking record owner or document a genuine exception.

o4 occurs in the signed 靈谷語錄序 by the lay author Ding Libiao (弟子丁立表題), and 自己 is in that author's first-person preface. Assigning Juelang Daosheng as utterer is wrong; Juelang is the person addressed and quoted later.

o6 is Wuzu Jie's quoted appraisal and o7 is Tianzhu Chonghui's direct answer; these support distinct grammatical deployments. The broad reflexive gloss holds, but 'personal realization' is imported terminology and should be replaced by the observable contrasts between one's own and another person's words/things.

The passages support a literal 'living road/open route,' but the prose's universal frame 'when a case has closed every fixed route' is not stated by the evidence. Several are formal-address declarations of an open road, not answers to a closed case.

o5 explicitly calls Shandao's 徑路修行 'this living road' and then challenges the assembly to go beyond it. That institutional Pure-Land route is a materially different referent from o1's ninety-day search for a route and o2's gods seeking a way out; test whether the current single sense is under-split rather than silently absorbing it into one Zen-loaded gloss.

Attribution generally holds for the direct record-owner addresses, but the explanation must distinguish direct speech, the quoted Meng'an Yue address, and Quanan Qiji's critical reuse rather than treating all six as one scenario.

o3 is first-person 行實 autobiography: the narrator says he received the novice ten precepts and was named Ruxi. Calling that voice an unnamed compiler leaves the source's named autobiographical subject/author unresolved.

o5 is procedural monastic-code prose in 沙彌受戒文, not ordinary compiler narration; its headword belongs to an instruction sequence (first five precepts, next ten) and needs an impersonal/editorial or exact compiler state supported by the source rather than the generic six-rung sentence.

The five witnesses consistently refer specifically to the novice's ten precepts (沙彌十戒), not an unspecified universal set of ten. Tighten the preferred target and explanation to that corpus fact; preserve the hard-rule/precepts carve-out without importing claims not anchored in these occurrences.

o2 is compiler narration ('元和中白居易出守茲郡'), not an unnamed monastic questioner. The question begins only after the narrator introduces Bai Juyi, so its ActorAttribution assigns the headword to the wrong grammatical actor.

o3 begins with narration and later has Bai identify himself as 白居易. If retained as one span, it contains both narrator and Bai voices; the headword-bearing occurrence must be cut or explicitly anchor which token supplies the evidence.
The Bai Juyi figure sense holds, but three witnesses repeat the same Bird's-Nest exchange. State the recurrence honestly and distinguish Bai's own quoted name/questions from compiler introductions.
o1 explicitly introduces Baoning Yong's snow hall address ('保寧勇禪師因雪，上堂') and the same named master performs 拍禪床 before descending. It is not an unnameable compiler action.

The other five named direct actions support the teaching-seat implementation and public-response prose. Repair o1's exact actor and add the section master to ContextMasters without changing the well-supported sense.

All six exact actors are named and the passages place the phrase beyond/before current temporal and teaching frames, but none of the selected occurrences defines Awesome-Voice as 'the earliest named Buddha.' That external superlative must be anchored from this corpus or removed.

The explanation says masters use it in questions whose answers test the demand, while the stored evidence consists chiefly of formal addresses, incense wording, and declarative contrasts. Describe those attested deployments instead of an absent question-answer pattern.
o3 repeats Juelang Daosheng's '撥轉上頭關捩子，大千法界現全機' address from another Juelang record, but labels the voice an unnamed compiler. The exact utterer is recoverable from the uninterrupted address.

The J34 and J25 witnesses are not independent semantic deployments merely because they have different work IDs: they reproduce the same speaker and wording. Re-grade source independence after controlling this duplicate-record family.

The pivotal-catch sense is supported by the remaining direct masters, but 'makes the whole exchange turn' is broader than several occurrences; tether the explanation to turning/operating the named 關捩 and the explicit failure of the mechanism to turn.
o5 is inside Chaozong Tongren's direct 小參: he himself says '又僧問雪峰：臨濟四喝...' and comments on it. It is not speech by an unnameable compiler.

o2 introduces a named commentary voice ('起綱宗云') before the headword, while o3 is compilation exposition. Resolve the named commentator and preserve the distinction between original question, later exposition, authored verse, and Chaozong's direct raising.

o1 is a signed 金陵語錄序 by the lay disciple Li Pan ('淮南弟子李盤拜題'), not an unnameable compiler. Its praise of Juelang must name Li Pan as exact author and Juelang as person described.
o3 is direct speech in Miyun Yuanwu's record explaining Mazu's great function/use, not compiler narration. The complete address identifies the record owner as utterer.

The gloss imports 'responsive capacity' and 'whole mechanism' where the sources variously praise a master's entire activity and demand great use. Tighten the inference to the observable 全/機/大用 wording and named deployments.

The explanation's central negative claim is false: o2 explicitly glosses the image in verse as '睦州檐板漢，擔來見一邊'—the board carrier carries it and sees one side. The entry says the witnesses do not supply a one-sided-vision gloss, but its own defining occurrence does.
Revise the interpretation from this corpus evidence, preserving the named stock phrase and explicitly anchoring the one-side inference to o2 rather than importing it from an outside dictionary.
o4 and o5 are later compiler/commentary uses, while o1 and o3 are direct Dahui and Liao'an deployments; keep those voice distinctions during repair.
o1 uses 種草 literally in '綠雖千種草，香祇一株蘭'; it does not denote lineage seed-stock. The entry merges an ordinary plant occurrence with the separately attested human/lineage-stock use.
Split or remove the literal witness, then re-test source depth for the Zen-loaded human-stock sense. The remaining passages support stock, seed, and succession language applied to people.
The six passages attest a public teaching-seat action, commonly immediately before 下座, but 'embodying the response' assigns an inward semantic job the action itself does not establish.
Describe the observable deployment: the master throws down the whisk to punctuate or terminate the address. Preserve the named actors and exact action anchors.

The hall/building sense holds, but the explanation claims the witnesses locate meetings and lodging there. The selected cases instead show institutional rules, incense/rite occasions, headings, and one answer naming the hall.
Rewrite the deployment account to match those observable institutional and ritual uses; do not infer lodging or meetings from the building label alone.
o3 is in a signed preface ending '住金陵比丘大成題'; the exact author is Dacheng, not Zongjian Falin. The book title names the compilation, not this headword's utterer.

The prose overstates a recurrent question-answer test: the evidence also includes appraisals, declarations, and compiler introduction. Retain the emergence/way-out sense but enumerate the attested deployment types.

Several occurrences are titled verses inside named masters' records and require recovery of the verse author rather than the generic compiler label; the current attribution review stops at the anthology surface.

The sources visibly raise, verse, or comment on the Devadatta-slanders-Buddha case. Tighten 'distinguished or implicated' to those observable deployments unless an explicit passage supplies that interpretive contrast.

o0 is direct incense-address wording by Zhufeng Min, not generic compiler narration. o2 stores overlapping evidence from the same passage and same work, so the pair is not two independent attestations.

The verse/portrait headings in o3-o4 also require author recovery from their named record contexts. Keep the distinct ordination-preceptor sense, deduplicate the Zhufeng witness, and refill depth from independent cases.
o4 occurs in an unnamed monk's direct question to Wuzu Fayan within Lingyin Xuanben's biography. Lingyin Xuanben is the section subject, not the utterer of the headword.
